subject.title: [Feature] Telegram Inline Query Support (@botname in any chat)

question: Should OpenClaw add Telegram inline queries as an opt-in bundled Telegram plugin ingress, and what authorization, privacy, session, cache, deadline, and chosen-result semantics are required?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but routing arbitrary-chat inline query text into tool-capable agents creates security and product-policy choices that code inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Sponsor a guarded inline-query design
options.body: Implement inline queries in the Telegram plugin behind explicit opt-in config with sender authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for sensitive answers, bounded execution, docs, focused tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer behind Guest Mode design
options.body: Wait for Guest Mode and bot-to-bot decisions to settle shared arbitrary-chat ingress primitives before accepting a separate inline-query implementation.

options.title: Decline built-in support for now
options.body: Leave inline queries to external plugin/API-extension discussion until maintainers decide the arbitrary-chat ingress and caching model belongs in core-bundled Telegram.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a guarded inline-query design
recommendation.body: Implement inline queries in the Telegram plugin behind explicit opt-in config with sender authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for sensitive answers, bounded execution, docs, focused tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Telegram handler/session work makes this the strongest routing candidate for the security-sensitive runtime design question.
